subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Prove that the angle of rotation of the axes to eliminate xy term from the equation ax²+2hxy+by²=0 is ½ Tan⁻¹(2h/(a−b)) where a ≠ b and π/4 if a = b.

mark_split.label: Set the XY coefficient to zero

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — say what 'eliminate the xy term' means as an equation, and say what happens when a equals b.

steps.label: Write the rotation formulas
steps.margin_note: First mark. Nothing here has numbers — the whole answer is carried in letters, so the two rotation formulas are written exactly as they stand.
steps.memory_tip: No numbers anywhere — the whole answer runs in letters, so write both rotation formulas exactly as they stand.
lines: Given original equation is  ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0  ……(1)
Angle of rotation is θ, then

recall.must_convey: That the general rotation formulas x = Xcosθ − Ysinθ, y = Ycosθ + Xsinθ are written for a general θ.
accept: write the rotation formulas with a general theta
x equals X cos theta minus Y sin theta and y equals Y cos theta plus X sin theta
take the angle of rotation as theta and write the standard formulas
theta ni general ga teesukoni rotation formulas rayali
the standard rotation formulas with theta

steps.why: This is a proof rather than a calculation, so θ has to stay a letter — the answer is a formula for θ, not a number.
common_mistakes: Putting a particular angle in for θ.
Getting the sign of the sine term wrong in x.

steps.label: Substitute and expand
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Substitute into (1) and expand all three terms. Only the XY parts matter for what follows, but the whole expansion is written out.
steps.memory_tip: Expand all three terms. Only the XY parts matter next, but the full expansion is what is marked.
lines: a(Xcosθ − Ysinθ)² + 2h(Xcosθ − Ysinθ)(Ycosθ + Xsinθ) + b(Ycosθ + Xsinθ)² = 0

recall.must_convey: That the rotation formulas are substituted into the given equation and all three terms expanded.
accept: substitute the rotation formulas into the given equation and expand every term
put x and y into a x squared plus two h x y plus b y squared
expand all three brackets in terms of capital X and Y
moodu terms ni expand cheyyali
substitute and expand fully

steps.why: The transformed equation has to be written out in full before the XY coefficient can be picked out of it.
common_mistakes: Expanding the squares but not the middle product.
Dropping the factor 2 in front of h.

steps.label: Set the XY coefficient to zero
steps.margin_note: Third mark, and the move the whole question turns on. Removing the xy term means its coefficient is zero — so collect every XY term from (2) and set that total to 0.
steps.memory_tip: Removing the xy term MEANS its coefficient is zero. Collect every XY term and set that total to 0.
lines: To remove the XY term, its coefficient in (2) must be zero:
⇒ −2a cosθ sinθ + 2h cos²θ − 2h sin²θ + 2b sinθ cosθ = 0

recall.must_convey: That the XY coefficient is collected and set to zero, and the double-angle identities turn it into sin2θ(b − a) + 2hcos2θ = 0.
accept: collect the X Y terms and set the coefficient to zero
eliminating the x y term means its coefficient is zero
use two sin cos is sin two theta and cos squared minus sin squared is cos two theta
X Y coefficient ni zero ga pettali
set the cross term coefficient equal to zero

steps.why: Eliminating a term is exactly the statement that its coefficient is zero — turning a word in the question into an equation is the whole step.
common_mistakes: Setting the whole transformed equation to zero instead of just the XY coefficient.

steps.label: Solve for θ
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Divide by cos2θ to get a tangent, then invert. The a = b case has to be handled separately, because the division by (a − b) is not allowed there.
steps.memory_tip: Divide by cos 2θ to get a tangent. The a = b case needs separate treatment — that division is illegal there.

lines.text: ∴ θ = ½ Tan⁻¹(2h/(a − b)),  and if a = b then θ = ½(π/2) = π/4

recall.must_convey: That dividing by cos2θ gives tan2θ = 2h/(a − b), so θ = ½Tan⁻¹(2h/(a − b)), and separately θ = π/4 when a = b.
accept: divide by cos two theta to get tan two theta equals two h over a minus b then halve the inverse tangent
theta is half tan inverse of two h by a minus b
when a equals b the tangent is undefined so two theta is ninety degrees and theta is pi by four
tan two theta equals two h by a minus b, theta half tan inverse
and if a equals b then theta is pi by four
heard_as: two h over a minus b

steps.why: The a = b case is not an afterthought: the division by (a − b) fails there, and 2h/0 sends 2θ to a right angle, so θ = π/4. The question asks for both branches.
common_mistakes: Giving θ = Tan⁻¹(2h/(a − b)) without the factor ½.
Omitting the a = b case that the question explicitly asks for.
